text: Zippo Pine Bar (1969–1998) is recognized as the leading Western Pleasure sire of Quarter Horses. He was a 1969 sorrel foal sired by Zippo Pat Bars and born from Dollie Pine, a daughter of Poco Pine, who in turn was a son of Poco Bueno. Dollie Pine’s mother was a descendant of Joe Moore, who was a half brother to Joe Reed P-3 and also a descendant of Traveler. Norman Reynolds purchased Zippo Pine Bar as a weanling at Lloyd Geweke's dispersal sale in 1969, with the intention of acquiring a halter horse. During his show career, he earned an AQHA Championship, a Performance Register of Merit, and a Superior Western Pleasure Horse Award. He was named the 1972 AQHA High Point Junior Western Pleasure Stallion and the 1972 AQHA High Point Junior Western Riding Horse. In 1992, he was inducted into the National Snaffle Bit Association Hall of Fame. He sired 1648 Quarter Horses, 68 Appaloosas, and 72 Paints, which together have accumulated over 50,000 show points. Five of his offspring—Mr Zippo Pine, Zippo By Moonlight, Zips Chocolate Chip, Zippos Mr Good Bar, and Zippos Amblin Easy—have been inducted into the NSBA Hall of Fame. His son Zippos Mr Good Bar was inducted into the AQHA Hall of Fame in 2019 and also into the National Snaffle Bit Association Hall of Fame in 2000. Other notable offspring include Melody Zipper, Flashy Zipper, Zippo Cash Bar, Zippo Jack Bar, Zippos Honeybee, and Don't Skip Zip. In 1991, his offspring won World Championships in Western Pleasure in the AQHA, the American Paint Horse Association (APHA), and the Appaloosa Horse Club (ApHC). Zippo Pine Bar was euthanized on January 12, 1998, at the age of 29 after suffering a major stroke. He was inducted into the AQHA Hall of Fame in 2000.
